problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}k \\ -3 \\ 1 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -3 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $a⊥b.$ Find the value of $k.$

feedback.problem: If $u=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]$ and $v=[\begin{aligned}k \\ 3 \\ -4 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ are orthogonal vectors, then $k=$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $u$ and $v$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that their dot product is equal to zero.
First, let's calculate the dot product in terms of $k$:

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}+{u}_{2}\cdot {v}_{2}+{u}_{3}\cdot {v}_{3}+{u}_{4}\cdot {v}_{4} \\  & =2\cdot k+(-3)\cdot 3+1\cdot (-4)+(-5)\cdot (-1) \\  & =2k-9-4+5 \\  & =2k-8\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the dot product to zero, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2k-8 & =0 \\ 2k & =8 \\ k & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
